summary:
San Luis Potosí sets its own rules on gender recognition, marriage and hate-crime aggravators within Mexico's national framework; the national layer is carried by the Mexico record. The state began authorising legal gender changes for transgender people on 17 May 2019, and is counted among the states that enacted a gender-identity law that year.

Partner recognition is settled at state level. The state Congress voted 14-12 on 16 May 2019 to approve same-sex marriage, which took effect on 21 May 2019, and joint adoption by same-sex couples became legal in the state in the same month. A trans visitor whose relationship would be read as same-sex under birth-sex status can therefore marry and be treated as a spouse here, and such couples can adopt jointly.

The state's hate-crime statute treats motivation by gender and sexual preference as an aggravating factor. On the source's wording the provision names gender and sexual preference rather than gender identity.

The state's anti-discrimination law bans discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender, but not gender identity. Gender-identity discrimination therefore falls outside the state's own prohibition even though the hate-crime statute reaches gender-based motivation.
tangentialFactors:
The margin on marriage was narrow: 14 votes to 12 in the state Congress on 16 May 2019, so the state's recognition of same-sex marriage and joint adoption rests on a contested vote rather than a broad consensus.

The state's two protection instruments use different categories. The hate-crime statute is keyed to gender and sexual preference, the anti-discrimination law to sexual orientation and gender, so which protection is available depends on the instrument a complaint is brought under.

Because joint adoption by same-sex couples is legal in the state, a trans visitor's partner and any children of the couple are recognised together, rather than recognition stopping at the marriage itself.
localsOnly:
Residents of San Luis Potosí have had access to a state legal gender-change procedure since 17 May 2019, and the state is counted among those that enacted a gender-identity law that year.

The state's anti-discrimination law covers sexual orientation and gender but not gender identity, so a resident complaining of gender-identity discrimination cannot rely on that statute. The hate-crime statute separately treats motivation by gender and sexual preference as an aggravating factor.

Joint adoption by same-sex couples has been legal in the state since May 2019, following the state Congress vote of 16 May 2019.
outOfScopeNotes:
No San Luis Potosí-specific enforcement data was identified. There is no record of prosecutions under the state hate-crime provision, no complaints data under the state anti-discrimination law, and no documented incidents of anti-trans violence in the state. Whether the 2019 recognition procedure operates in practice without medical requirements, fees or delays is not sourced.

The state-level facts rest on a Mexico-wide reference article rather than the statutory texts, so the exact wording of the anti-discrimination and hate-crime provisions is not quoted. National counts of states with gender-recognition procedures, and national-level violence and oversight findings, belong to the Mexico record and are not repeated here.
